The Animated Zoo · written Nov 16, 2026

The story world and the cartoon style

Who lives in the zoo, where the adventures go, and how every cartoon video is drawn. Every picture on this page comes from the same drawing code the videos use, so a character cannot look different in a video than it does here.

Grown-ups: Mama Elephant (warm, slow, kind) and Sandy's Mama. The voices are made by the studio's own voice engine. I checked that every word can be placed from the audio; I cannot listen, so how the voices sound to the ear is for you to judge in the test adventure.

The world

The zoo gate is home. Every adventure starts and ends there. From the gate the friends go out to one place and come back before the sun goes down.

Same every time

  • The hook, then Milo: "I'm Milo! Come on a big adventure with us!"
  • The refrain on the way out and on the way home: "Friends help friends, come along with me!"
  • The ending song line: "Friends help friends, hooray, hooray! What a big adventure day!"
  • Milo's goodbye: "See you on the next adventure, friends!"

New every time

  • One place and one friend who lives there.
  • One problem a small child knows: a present, a shy feeling, something too high, too far, too hot.
  • Two or three true things about the animals, each one used to solve the problem.

Always true of the world

  • Kindness, courage, friendship, curiosity.
  • No villains and no danger. Nobody is hurt, lost, crying or trapped.
  • The night forest is cosy and bright enough to see every face.
  • The friends solve the problem themselves.

Character sheets

Line, shape and shading

Shape

  • Everything is built from round shapes. No sharp corners on a character.
  • Babies have a big head and big eyes for their body.
  • Eyes: a white circle, a brown iris, a dark pupil, two white sparkles. The same eye on every animal.
  • A pink cheek on every face.

Line

  • One outline round the whole silhouette, 9 units wide, in a dark shade of the animal's own colour. Never black.
  • Every part that moves carries its own outline, so a head that turns or a trunk that lifts takes its line with it.
  • No outlines on backgrounds: the characters stand out because only they have a line.

Shading

  • Flat colour. One soft highlight on top, one darker crescent under the belly, a soft shadow on the ground.
  • No gradients on characters. Skies are the only gradient.
  • Legs on the far side are one step darker.

Words on screen

  • One typeface: Baloo 2, extra bold, for every word in the picture.
  • Three word styles: white with a dark outline; sun yellow with a dark outline for the key word; dark on a yellow pill for names and labels.
  • Words never cover a face, never touch the watermark, never sit on the caption, and are never cut by the frame.
  • A word appears on the spoken word, placed from the audio.

Camera and transitions

  • Cut between shots in the same place. Every shot drifts a little, in or out, so the picture is never frozen.
  • Iris (a yellow circle with a blue ring that opens and closes, with a soft whoosh) only when the place changes.
  • Close-ups show a face, a detail, or a part of the body the line is about. A second character is either whole in the picture or not in it.
  • The tall version of a shot has its own camera, its own word positions and, where needed, its own prop positions.

Watermark

  • It is drawn into the video, because YouTube's own watermark button is not available on videos made for kids.
  • Nothing that matters sits under it: no face, no word, no answer sign.
  • Thumbnails carry no mark.
